title: Restriction of scalars is left adjoint to coextension
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-modobj-coextension], let $\varphi$ be a morphism of monoid
objects. Let $\varepsilon_N\colon\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)\to N$ be evaluation at
the unit of $\mathcal S$. Then $\varepsilon_N$ is $\mathcal R$-linear on
$\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)$
([def-sfb-modobj-restriction]). Moreover, $g\mapsto\varepsilon_N\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(g)$
is a bijection, natural in $M$ and $N$, from $\mathcal S$-linear maps
$M\to\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi N$ to $\mathcal R$-linear maps
$\operatorname{Res}_\varphi M\to N$. Its inverse sends $f$ to $m\mapsto(s\mapsto f(sm))$.
This is an adjunction
$$
\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi .
$$

proof.text:
Put $H_N=\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi N$, with equalizer inclusion $i_N:H_N\to\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal S,N)$ and evaluation $e_N:\mathcal S\otimes H_N\to N$, as in [def-sfb-modobj-coextension]. Write $a=\mu_{\mathcal S}\circ(\varphi\otimes\mathcal S)$. For any object $Y$, curry a map $b:\mathcal S\otimes Y\to N$. Its transpose factors uniquely through $i_N$ precisely when
$$b\circ(a\otimes1_Y)=\gamma_N\circ(1_{\mathcal R}\otimes b)\circ\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal S,Y}.$$
Explicitly, let $p,q$ denote the first and second equalizer arrows in [def-sfb-modobj-coextension], and put $c=\operatorname{curry}(b)$. Naturality of evaluation and the definitions of $p,q$ give
$$\operatorname{uncurry}(p\circ c)=b\circ(a\otimes1_Y),\qquad
\operatorname{uncurry}(q\circ c)=\gamma_N\circ(1_{\mathcal R}\otimes b)\circ\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal S,Y}.$$
The first substitutes the source action $a$ into evaluation; the second substitutes $c$ into the defining evaluation composite for $q$ and uses $\mathrm{ev}\circ(1_{\mathcal S}\otimes c)=b$. Thus injectivity of uncurrying identifies the equalizer equation $p\circ c=q\circ c$ with the displayed condition. The equalizer universal property gives the unique factorization. Also maps $u,v:Y\to H_N$ are equal if $e_N(1_{\mathcal S}\otimes u)=e_N(1_{\mathcal S}\otimes v)$: injectivity of transposition gives $i_Nu=i_Nv$; then $u$ and $v$ are two factorizations of the same equalizing arrow through $i_N$, so the uniqueness part of the equalizer universal property gives $u=v$. Below, expressions $b(s,y)$ denote these morphisms on ordered tensor factors, with the displayed associators and unitors understood; no assertion that elements separate morphisms is used.

source.place: Coextension definition: closedness and equalizer; preliminary interpretation of the inverse formula

proof.text:
Define $\varepsilon_N=e_N\circ(\eta_{\mathcal S}\otimes1_{H_N})\circ\lambda_{H_N}^{-1}$. By [def-sfb-modobj-coextension] the action satisfies $e_N(t,s\cdot h)=e_N(ts,h)$ and the equalizer condition says $e_N(\varphi(r)t,h)=r\cdot e_N(t,h)$. Set $t=1$, by precomposing with the unit in the test factor, to obtain
$$\varepsilon_N(\varphi(r)\cdot h)=e_N(\varphi(r),h)=r\cdot\varepsilon_N(h).$$
This is equality of morphisms $\mathcal R\otimes H_N\to N$, using the unit laws. The action on the source is the restricted action of [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], so $\varepsilon_N:\operatorname{Res}_\varphi H_N\to N$ is $\mathcal R$-linear.

source.place: Statement: evaluation at the unit is R-linear (agent expansion)

proof.text:
For an $\mathcal S$-linear $g:M\to H_N$, restriction makes $g$ an $\mathcal R$-linear map by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. Compose it with the $\mathcal R$-linear $\varepsilon_N$ of step 2. Composition in the module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] therefore defines
$$A_{M,N}(g)=\varepsilon_N\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(g):\operatorname{Res}_\varphi M\to N.$$

source.place: Statement: the forward map g to evaluation composed with restriction

proof.text:
For an $\mathcal R$-linear $f:\operatorname{Res}_\varphi M\to N$, form the actual morphism $b_f=f\circ\gamma_M:\mathcal S\otimes M\to N$. Module associativity [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and $\mathcal R$-linearity for the restricted action [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] give, on $\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal S\otimes M$,
$$b_f(\varphi(r)s,m)=f((\varphi(r)s)m)=f(\varphi(r)(sm))=r\cdot f(sm)=r\cdot b_f(s,m).$$
Thus $b_f$ satisfies exactly the equalizer criterion in step 1, for the equalizer of [def-sfb-modobj-coextension]. It defines a unique underlying morphism $B_{M,N}(f):M\to H_N$ with $e_N(s,B_{M,N}(f)(m))=f(sm)$.

source.place: Statement: inverse formula, factorization through the equalizer (agent expansion)

proof.text:
The morphism of step 4 is $\mathcal S$-linear. To compare $B(f)\circ\gamma_M$ and the action on $H_N$ composed with $1_{\mathcal S}\otimes B(f)$, use the extensionality criterion of step 1. Their evaluations on the ordered factors $\mathcal S\otimes\mathcal S\otimes M$ are
$$e_N(t,B(f)(sm))=f(t(sm))=f((ts)m)=e_N(ts,B(f)(m))=e_N(t,s\cdot B(f)(m)).$$
The middle equality is the module associativity law of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and the last equality is precisely the source-right-multiplication action of [def-sfb-modobj-coextension]. This proves linearity, without exchanging the two $\mathcal S$ factors.

source.place: Statement: inverse formula gives an S-linear morphism (agent expansion)

proof.text:
The two maps are inverse. By the module unit law [sk-def-sfb-module-objects],
$$A(B(f))(m)=e_N(1,B(f)(m))=f(1m)=f(m).$$
For $\mathcal S$-linear $g:M\to H_N$, its linearity and the action formula of [def-sfb-modobj-coextension] give
$$e_N(s,B(A(g))(m))=A(g)(sm)=e_N(1,g(sm))=e_N(1,s\cdot g(m))=e_N(s,g(m)).$$
Here the final equality uses $1s=s$. Extensionality from step 1 now gives $B(A(g))=g$ as underlying morphisms, hence as module morphisms by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Thus $A$ is a bijection with inverse $B$.

source.place: Statement: bijection with the specified inverse (agent expansion)

proof.text:
Check naturality explicitly. For $\mathcal S$-linear $u:M'\to M$ and $\mathcal R$-linear $v:N\to N'$, write $H(v):H_N\to H_{N'}$ for coextension on morphisms. Restriction leaves underlying maps unchanged [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], while $H(v)$ is postcomposition [def-sfb-modobj-coextension]. Consequently
$$A_{M',N}(g\circ u)=A_{M,N}(g)\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(u),\qquad A_{M,N'}(H(v)\circ g)=v\circ A_{M,N}(g).$$
The first is associativity of composition; for the second both sides evaluate $g(m)$ at $1$ and then apply $v$. For the inverse maps the evaluation formulas are
$$e_N(s,B(f\circ\operatorname{Res}_\varphi u)(m'))=f(u(sm'))=f(su(m'))=e_N(s,B(f)(u(m'))),$$
$$e_{N'}(s,B(v\circ f)(m))=v(f(sm))=e_{N'}(s,H(v)(B(f)(m))).$$
The first uses the definition of module morphism [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; the second uses postcomposition. By step 1 these are the naturality identities for $B$.

source.place: Statement: naturality in M and N (agent expansion)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] with $F=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$, $G=\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi$ and $\Psi_{M,N}=B_{M,N}=A_{M,N}^{-1}$. Steps 3--7 give the required bijections and both naturality laws, for the functors [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] and [def-sfb-modobj-coextension]. Therefore $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\dashv\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi$. Its counit at $N$ is $A_{H_N,N}(1_{H_N})=\varepsilon_N$, so the adjunction is the specified one.

split_report.summary: Expanded the internal-Hom/equalizer argument into eight steps: tensor-valued factorization and extensionality, R-linearity of unit evaluation, forward map, construction and S-linearity of the inverse, both inverse identities, both naturality laws, and the adjunction. Reused the existing natural-bijection Mathlib leaf and two scalar-change definitions plus the module-object definition. No new nodes and no hypotheses or statement changes. Checked both semantic phrasings and local Mathlib candidates; ordinary ring modules and representations do not cover the general monoidal statement. Revalidated the inherited split against the now-reviewed coextension statement and refreshed stale citation excerpts; repeated the prescribed searches with two internal-module phrasings. Second reading made equalizer cancellation explicit and corrected step source locators to the actual statement clauses; independently searched the inverse/currying formulation.
